original_card.question: Does one selected supplier obligation follow from its actual source-bound checks?
methods: Trace one hypothesis through the source, checker and complete caller.
Construct one semantically invalid but superficially well-formed fixture and test rejection.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Pin the current sources and one obligation; the historical owner audit is an example, not evidence of a current bug.

first_step.inspect: Identify why the timing-only omission passes but the full production controller still rejects it.

original_card.first_experiment: Choose one current supplier obligation and trace whether its acceptance depends on an independent check.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Closing a current acceptance gap or proof obligation strengthens reliability even without changing kappa.
allowed_variations: Audit one named current condition using a new semantic counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Reporting the historical timing-only diagnostic as a new current acceptance bug.

actual_scope: On the selected PR1094 sixteen-replica owner map, cross-child pending-axis disjointness does not follow from the role audit or from the rebuilt port-basis chart predicate. The pinned phase file itself satisfies the obligation.
scope_change_reason: The card allows one named current condition and a new semantic counterexample. The condition is X2 for the selected T16 map. The historical PR626 timing-only bridge omission is only the orientation example and is not reported as a current acceptance bug.
bottleneck_link: The selected complex supplier is the binding side. Its idle-remainder accounting uses pending axes of distinct children on one physical family. A role or chart pass does not establish that separation, so a later packing change can keep a legal-looking chart while sharing an axis. No new kappa is claimed.
stop_rule: One obligation, the published map, and one idle-suffix axis transplant. No parameter search and no selected cold replay.
evidence: PASS_SELECTED_T16_AXIS_DISJOINTNESS_GAP. Published map: 2016 X2 checks pass, 69120 charts accept, 0 hosted-axis collisions, deficit 5120. Transplant of axis 2^49 from child 11 index 0 into child 10 index 0 at pair 3, side 1, port 0: X2 rejects, all 69120 rebuilt charts stay identical, role audit still accepts. Duplicate-inside-slice control rejects 16 charts. One discussion comment on 1166 was forbidden and was not retried. The selected cold replay was not run.

open_questions.question: Does the emitted idle-remainder frame export, or only the separate X2 scan, reject this same idle-suffix transplant when the phase hash pin is deliberately not used?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The selected replay hash-pins DATA-PHASES.json, so a substituted file fails closed before the semantic checks. That pin does not show whether the controller's remainder frames themselves enforce disjointness.
open_questions.first_step: Recompute only the literal idle-remainder tails for child 10 at port 0 from the transplanted axes and compare them with the tails from the pinned phase, without running make frontier1094-verify.
open_questions.blocked_by: The emitted GLOBAL-TEMPLATE and IDLE-REMAINDER-FRAMES are produced by the cold replay, which this package does not run.
